questions.question: 1. When break is encountered inside any loop, control automatically passes to the beginning of the loop.

explanations.a: Incorrect. A break exits the current loop immediately instead of restarting it.
explanations.b: Correct. The break statement exits the loop and does not return to the beginning.

questions.question: 2. Which of the following is not a loop in C?

explanations.a: Correct. 'Repeat' is not a standard loop construct in C.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This is a valid loop structure in C, though it is evaluated after the body runs once.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This is a standard repetition construct used for conditional iteration.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is a standard loop used when the iteration count is known.

questions.question: 9. Which of the following is an exit-controlled loop?

explanations.a: Incorrect. A for loop checks the condition before each iteration begins.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A while loop evaluates its condition before the body executes.
explanations.c: Correct. 'Do-While' is an exit-controlled loop because the condition is checked after the body.
explanations.d: Incorrect. One of the standard loop types is exit-controlled.

questions.question: 10. Which among the following is an unconditional control structure?

explanations.a: Correct. 'Goto' is an unconditional control structure as it transfers control unconditionally.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This statement jumps out of a loop or switch rather than transferring control unconditionally.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This keyword skips the remaining body and continues to the next iteration.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This is a conditional branch structure, not an unconditional jump.
